topic.title: Graph Neural Expressivity and Generalization
topic.overview: Graph neural networks must represent structure without depending on arbitrary node order. This topic studies the limits of message passing and the benefits of subgraphs, positional encodings, higher-order constructions, and implicit graph representations. Being able to distinguish more graphs is only one part of successful learning.
topic.whyItMatters: Extra expressivity may increase cost or fit distinctions irrelevant to a task. Generalization analysis asks when richer structure actually improves predictive margins or sample efficiency rather than merely passing an isomorphism test.
topic.evolution: The representatives include early learned graph encodings, then formal comparisons of modern graph-network extensions. Recent studies connect expressivity with generalization and investigate truncated positional information. Work on random features for implicit graphs also targets computation without materializing every edge. Together these threads link representational power with the statistical and computational conditions under which it is useful.
openQuestions: When do higher-order structures improve generalization enough to justify their cost?
Which positional encodings remain stable across graph size and sampling changes?

papers.title: TopoTune: A Framework for Generalized Combinatorial Complex Neural Networks
papers.tldr: TopoTune supports a generalized family of topological neural networks that subsumes CCNNs and often matches or improves their performance with less complexity.

papers.title: Uncertainty Estimation for Heterophilic Graphs Through the Lens of Information Theory
papers.tldr: Combining node representations across layers improves uncertainty estimation on heterophilic graphs, supported by information-theoretic analysis and experiments.

papers.title: Weisfeiler and Leman Go Gambling: Why Expressive Lottery Tickets Win
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditions for sparse GNNs to preserve full-network expressivity and links expressive initialization to potential learning benefits.

papers.title: What Makes a Good Feedforward Computational Graph?
papers.tldr: Fidelity and mixing time provide complementary measures for analyzing feedforward computational graphs and their relationship to trained-network performance.

papers.title: WILTing Trees: Interpreting the Distance Between MPNN Embeddings
papers.tldr: WILT-based distances explain graph-network embedding geometry through a small set of task-relevant subgraphs.

papers.title: Bridging Theory and Practice in Link Representation with Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: A link-level expressiveness framework shows why more powerful graph models become especially useful as graph symmetry increases.

papers.title: Equivariance Everywhere All At Once: A Recipe for Graph Foundation Models
papers.tldr: A symmetry-based architecture recipe produces graph models with strong reported zero-shot node classification across diverse datasets.

papers.title: Higher-Order Learning with Graph Neural Networks via Hypergraph Encodings
papers.tldr: Hypergraph structural encodings increase graph neural networks’ representational power and improve performance on both graph and hypergraph datasets.

papers.title: Logical Expressiveness of Graph Neural Networks with Hierarchical Node Individualization
papers.tldr: HE-GNNs form an increasingly expressive graph-network hierarchy with a logical characterization on bounded-degree graphs and demonstrated practical benefits.

papers.title: MIHC: Multi-View Interpretable Hypergraph Neural Networks with Information Bottleneck for Chip Congestion Prediction
papers.tldr: MIHC combines circuit graphs and images in a hypergraph model that improves congestion prediction and identifies informative circuit regions.

papers.title: Random Search Neural Networks for Efficient and Expressive Graph Learning
papers.tldr: Random search neural networks improve graph coverage and expressivity, matching or exceeding random-walk performance with up to 16 times fewer sequences.

papers.title: Return of ChebNet: Understanding and Improving an Overlooked GNN on Long Range Tasks
papers.tldr: Stable-ChebNet stabilizes an early spectral graph network’s dynamics, achieving near state-of-the-art performance on long-range graph tasks.

papers.title: Sound Logical Explanations for Mean Aggregation Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: The paper establishes sound logical explanations for mean-aggregation GNNs with non-negative weights and shows that these explanations can reveal model issues.

papers.title: Understanding and Enhancing Message Passing on Heterophilic Graphs via Compatibility Matrix
papers.tldr: CMGNN uses compatibility-matrix discriminability to explain and improve message passing on graphs with dissimilar neighbors.

papers.title: What Expressivity Theory Misses: Message Passing Complexity for GNNs
papers.tldr: Message Passing Complexity measures task difficulty for graph neural networks beyond the binary distinctions of expressivity theory.

papers.title: A Graphop Analysis of Graph Neural Networks on Sparse Graphs: Generalization and Universal Approximation
papers.tldr: A graphop-based framework strengthens approximation and generalization theory for message passing networks on sparse and dense graphs of arbitrary size.

papers.title: A Unifying Relational Perspective on Expressive Lottery Tickets
papers.tldr: The paper establishes conditional expressivity guarantees and random-pruning probability bounds for sparse relational and temporal graph networks.

papers.title: Anchor-guided Hypergraph Condensation with Dual-level Discrimination
papers.tldr: AHGCDD condenses hypergraphs by jointly refining synthetic features and relationships while reducing repeated neural-network training.

papers.title: Expressive Graph Neural Networks via Equivariant Use of Noise
papers.tldr: ENGNNs use noise equivariantly to combine universal graph expressivity, reduced theoretical sample complexity, and practical message-passing scalability.

papers.title: Graph Neural Networks Are Not Continuous Across Graph Resolutions
papers.tldr: The paper identifies why standard GNNs can produce incompatible embeddings across graph resolutions and derives an architectural modification that restores continuity across scales.

papers.title: InvGNN: Learning Invertible Node Representations on Graphs
papers.tldr: InvGNN builds fully invertible graph networks that retain 1-WL-level expressiveness and support classification, density estimation, and generation.

papers.title: Kronecker Generative Networks: A General Neural Architecture for Parameter-Efficient Learning Across Classification Tasks
papers.tldr: Kronecker Generative Networks use recursive rules to build controllable connectivity patterns, yielding favorable accuracy–efficiency trade-offs across classification domains.

papers.title: Learning to Execute Graph Algorithms Exactly with Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Under bounded-degree and finite-precision constraints, learned local update rules enable exact graph-algorithm execution with high probability.

papers.title: Message Passing on the Edge: Towards Scalable and Expressive GNNs
papers.tldr: EB-GNN passes messages through edges and triangles to gain stronger graph expressivity while retaining near-linear costs on practical workloads.

papers.title: Position: Graph Condensation Needs a Reset—Move Beyond Full-dataset Training and Model-Dependence
papers.tldr: Graph condensation should prioritize total resource savings and cross-architecture usefulness instead of costly, model-dependent compression.

papers.title: Pruning at Initialisation through the lens of Graphon Limit: Convergence, Expressivity, and Generalisation
papers.tldr: Graphon limits characterize initialization-time pruning patterns and connect sparse topology to approximation and conditional generalization results.

papers.title: SWING: Unlocking Implicit Graph Representations for Graph Random Features
papers.tldr: SWING approximates Graph Random Feature computations through continuous-space walks, avoiding explicit construction of feature-defined graphs.

papers.title: Understanding Truncated Positional Encodings for Graph Neural Networks
papers.tldr: Truncation breaks expressivity equivalences between graph positional encodings, and experiments favor combining truncated families.

papers.title: Which Algorithms Can Graph Neural Networks Learn?
papers.tldr: The paper gives sufficient conditions for graph networks to learn algorithms that generalize to arbitrary input sizes, alongside impossibility results and architectural remedies.
